newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $68, passed - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $68, passed - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle bids at $68.00 per cwt were passed by owners pricing cattle at $69.00 to $70.00, feedlot sources said.
Bids at $68.00 were unchanged from last week's active sales amd widespread in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area and Kansas.

Several feedlot operators were optimistic about the firm bids, which they said suggested that packers need cattle to fill retail beef orders despite hefty cattle sales last week. They did not foresee sales until midweek because higher bids would probably spur owners to hold cattle more tightly.
"They'll probably want to fight us for a day, or two, because if they bid $69.00 today, they would have to pay $70.00," one Kansas feedyard manager said.

Fed cattle prices this week were seen supported by outlooks for continued strong beef demand, cattle feeders said. Beef demand was seen firm the next few weeks as retailers book orders for outdoor grilling beef promotions and for upcoming holiday advertising features.
Fed cattle prices also could be buoyed by projections for steady to smaller showlists this week than last week, several sources said.
